value.body: A two-year master's degree covering classical and quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, statistical physics, mathematical methods and a specialisation such as condensed matter, nuclear and particle physics, astrophysics or electronics. It usually includes lab work and often a project. It leads to research, teaching and some technical industry roles.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc with physics (and usually mathematics). IITs, IISc and some other institutes admit through IIT JAM; central and many state universities use CUET-PG; others run their own tests. JEST is used by several research institutes for integrated PhD programmes.

value.title: At a glance
items: The research route usually runs through CSIR-UGC NET, GATE or JEST to a PhD.
College teaching usually needs NET and, for many posts, a PhD.
Industry roles (data, electronics, instrumentation) often value programming and lab skills alongside the degree.
